mediaWork.title: The Thin Blue Line
mediaWork.publisherOrNetwork: American Playhouse, Third Floor Productions, Miramax
mediaWork.focusOrTheme: Wrongful conviction, murder case investigation, reliability of testimony, impact of filmmaking on justice.
mediaWork.summaryNotes: Errol Morris's unique documentary dramatically re-enacts the crime scene and investigation of a Dallas police officer's murder. It successfully argues that a man was wrongly convicted for the crime by a corrupt justice system in Dallas County, Texas.

mediaItems.focusOrTheme: Wrongful conviction, murder case investigation, reliability of testimony, impact of filmmaking on justice.
mediaItems.summaryNotes: Errol Morris's documentary deconstructs the case against Randall Dale Adams, who was convicted based on the testimony of David Ray Harris. The film exposed contradictions and unreliable witnesses, leading to Adams's exoneration.

featuredIndividuals.narrativeSummary: Convicted of capital murder based on perjured testimony and flawed eyewitness identifications. Served approximately 12 years before his conviction was overturned. He was later exonerated after the film exposed issues with his case.
